works.alt: Seen from above, a woman in a striped dress supports a child on her lap and washes a small foot in a basin. A white pitcher stands beside them.
looking: Follow the two hands: one steadies the child, one cups a foot.
Compare the oval basin with the rounded opening of the pitcher.
works.context: Cassatt used a steep viewpoint and abundant pattern in this scene of a caregiver and child. The museum connects these choices to her engagement with Japanese art in the 1890s.
noted_details: One hand rests across the child’s waist; the other holds a foot inside the basin.
Long stripes in the dress bend around the seated figures.
The white basin and pitcher repeat rounded openings near the bottom of the painting.
works.title: The Child's Bath

works.alt: Workers sit in a dark Venetian workshop, handling bundles of long, pale glass canes. Light enters at the upper left and catches the rods and a white blouse.
looking: Follow the pale glass canes from the foreground back to the workers’ hands.
Look for the brightest painted stroke in this mostly dark room.
works.context: Sargent painted Venetian glass-bead workers in the early 1880s. The museum identifies the pale rods as glass canes, prepared for cutting into beads, then polishing and stringing into jewelry.
noted_details: Pale green and white rods form several fans against the dark room.
The worker on the right holds glass near a small upright tool.
The window occupies only the upper-left corner, while light reappears across hands, clothing, and glass.
works.title: Venetian Glass Workers
Burden Basket
works.alt: A tan woven basket widens from a narrow base to an open rim, with repeating dark-brown triangles across its sides.
looking: Choose one triangle and follow the repeating pattern around the basket.
Notice how the form widens from its base towards the rim.
works.context: This Pomo basket from Northern California was made for practical use. Its diagonal twining carries triangular patterns that grow larger as the woven form widens toward its open rim.
noted_details: Dark triangles grow larger as they rise from the narrow base.
Bands of smaller triangles make zigzag paths between the larger shapes.
The broad oval rim exposes the fine, paler weave inside the basket.

works.alt: A diamond-shaped white canvas contains horizontal and vertical black lines, a large yellow triangle at left, a blue wedge at right, a black rectangle, and a tiny red triangle below.
looking: Follow a black line until it stops. Does it meet the edge?
Compare the small red triangle with the much larger yellow and blue areas.
works.context: Mondrian rotated the square canvas while keeping its internal lines horizontal and vertical. The museum reads this as an exploration of the relationship between a painting and its enclosing edges.
noted_details: The diamond’s slanted perimeter surrounds a level horizontal and vertical grid.
A small red wedge sits near the lower-left edge, below a broad black horizontal line.
Several black lines stop before the border, while the long line above the blue reaches the sloping right edge.
works.title: Lozenge Composition with Yellow, Black, Blue, Red, and Gray

works.alt: An empty grey room contains a keyboard instrument, a chair, and a stringed instrument leaning at the right. A small framed picture hangs within a much larger rectangle of wall moulding.
looking: Compare the small picture frame with the much larger rectangle around it.
Find the diagonal instrument among the room’s upright and level lines.
works.context: Hammershøi repeatedly painted rooms in the Copenhagen apartment he shared with Ida. The museum describes furniture and objects rearranged for pictorial effect, with light entering from a window outside this composition.
noted_details: A small dark picture frame sits inside a large rectangle of pale wall moulding.
An empty chair stands in front of the keyboard, partly overlapping it.
The stringed instrument leans diagonally beside the keyboard; the surrounding architecture stays mostly upright.
works.title: Interior. The Music Room, Strandgade 30
